name: Ed Elson
summary: Ed Elson is named in 3 Parts of The Buildout, most recently Part 16: The Seller Holds the Paper. Argued in Part 5 (Voices that cross sides), Part 14 (The bill has moved to debt), Part 16 (Two labs carry the chain).

parts.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Are Not the Same Business

mentions.excerpt: Ed Elson’s view of unsustainable Big Tech growth requires frontier labs to remain structurally loss-making.

mentions.section: The bill has moved to debt
mentions.excerpt: Ed Elson of Prof G Markets noted on August 11 that Google had spent $45 billion and Amazon $54 billion in a single quarter and that both ended with negative cash flow.

Ed Elson of Prof G Markets estimated on July 7 that the two labs supplied 60% to 80% of the AI revenue at Amazon, Google and Microsoft and, citing The Information, about half of the hyperscalers' revenue backlog.

sides.claim: Because OpenAI and Anthropic pay their bills with venture funding of which Big Tech supplies roughly 40%, revenue Big Tech books from them is partly recycled from itself and not real growth.
If Big Tech depends heavily on OpenAI and Anthropic for revenue growth, that growth is unsustainable because both customers are massively unprofitable and may not survive.

sides.sideLabel: The bill has moved to debt
sides.claim: Google spent $45 billion and Amazon $54 billion on capital expenditures in a single quarter, and both ended up with negative cash flows despite huge cash intake.
